paragraphs.title: Wealth Without Enjoyment and the Superiority of the Stillborn

answers: Riches, wealth, and honour
Wisdom, strength, and rule
Poverty, sickness, and loneliness
easy.explanation: The verse says God gave him riches, wealth, and honour.
easy.q: What had God given the man described in verse 2?

answers: See the sun
Eat thereof
Live many years
easy.explanation: God did not give him power to eat thereof; a stranger ate it.
easy.q: What was the man unable to do with his possessions?

answers: The wise man
The rich man
An untimely birth
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says the untimely birth hath more rest than he.
easy.q: Who is said to have more rest than the man with wealth and long life?

answers: He cannot enjoy what he possesses
He has no wealth at all
He lives only a short time
medium.explanation: Although he has abundance, he cannot eat thereof or enjoy it.
medium.q: Why is the wealthy man's situation called vanity and an evil disease?

answers: The life of a wise man
The state of an untimely birth
The life of a man with a hundred children and many years
medium.explanation: The passage describes a man with children and long life whose soul is not filled with good.
medium.q: What situation is compared with having a long life but no good or burial?

answers: A man who fell on the road
A child who did not experience earthly life
A man who lost his wealth
medium.explanation: The untimely birth comes in vanity and departs in darkness without experiencing life.
medium.q: What does “an untimely birth” refer to in this passage?

answers: Both possess riches and honour
Neither necessarily experiences the benefits of life
Both live two thousand years
challenge.explanation: The wealthy man cannot enjoy his possessions, while the untimely birth avoids life's burdens and disappointments.
challenge.q: What is the central comparison between the wealthy man and the untimely birth?

answers: The man cannot count his days
Long life is useless if the soul is not filled with good
Every man must die immediately
challenge.explanation: Even two thousand years are said to bring no good when the soul remains unsatisfied.
challenge.q: Why is long life not presented as sufficient advantage?

answers: Outward abundance alone does not guarantee satisfaction
Only riches bring rest
Life is always better than death
challenge.explanation: The passage shows that possessions and honour are insufficient without the power to enjoy them.
challenge.q: What principle emerges from the contrast between wealth and enjoyment?

answers: His mouth
Changing the world
Obtaining immortality
easy.explanation: The verse says, “All the labour of man is for his mouth.”
easy.q: What is all the labour of man for, according to verse 7?

answers: It is completely filled
It is not filled
It ceases to exist
easy.explanation: The verse says, “yet the appetite is not filled.”
easy.q: What happens to the appetite despite all human labour?

answers: Whether only the wise can enjoy life
Whether only the fool labours
What the wise has more than the fool
easy.explanation: Verse 8 asks, “For what hath the wise more than the fool?”
easy.q: What question does Qohelet ask about the wise and the fool?

answers: Labour satisfies every desire
Labour meets needs but does not guarantee inner satisfaction
Labour prevents a man from eating
medium.explanation: Human labour is directed toward the mouth, yet the appetite remains unfilled.
medium.q: What relationship does the passage show between labour and satisfaction?

answers: It is better to value what is present than chase unattained desires
It is better to stop seeing reality
It is better to dream only about the future
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts present sight with restless desire.
medium.q: What does “Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire” suggest?

answers: Something unable to provide lasting meaning or satisfaction
Great wealth
Deep wisdom
medium.explanation: Even preferring what is before the eyes is not a complete answer to human dissatisfaction.
medium.q: What does “vanity” mean in “this is also vanity”?

answers: Even present reality is subject to vanity and vexation of spirit
A person cannot see anything
The appetite is always satisfied
challenge.explanation: The verse concludes that this preference is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
challenge.q: Why is even the sight of the eyes not presented as a perfect solution?

answers: The tension between attending to reality and pursuing unattained desires
The tension between wealth and poverty only
The tension between wisdom and foreknowledge
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts what is directly present with desire that wanders beyond it.
challenge.q: What tension is expressed between “the sight of the eyes” and “the wandering of the desire”?

answers: Wisdom alone does not remove the limits of human life
The fool knows everything
The wise man does not need food
challenge.explanation: Both wise and foolish people remain subject to labour, desire, and mortality.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the question, “What hath the wise more than the fool?”

answers: That he is an angel
That he is man
That he has unlimited power
easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “it is known that it is man.”
easy.q: What has already been named and made known about man?

answers: With him that is mightier than he
With himself only
With one weaker than he
easy.explanation: The verse says man may not contend with him that is mightier than he.
easy.q: With whom may man not contend?

answers: Vanity
Immortality
The fullness of the soul
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says that many things increase vanity.

answers: He is only man, and reality is mightier than he
There is no reality in the world
He knows the entire future
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes man's limited strength before what is mightier than he.
medium.q: Why can man not change what has already been established?

answers: More possibilities always create meaning
Many things can multiply distractions and vanity
Many things remove the need for man
medium.explanation: The verse directly says that many things increase vanity.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between many things and vanity?

answers: Stronger or more powerful
Younger
Nearer
medium.explanation: Mightier describes one possessing greater strength or authority.
medium.q: What does “mightier” mean in “him that is mightier than he”?

answers: Man cannot contend with or reshape what is stronger than he
Man cannot speak
Man does not know that he is man
challenge.explanation: Man is identified as human, but he cannot contend with the mightier power.
challenge.q: What human limitation is emphasized in verse 10?

answers: It shows that many possibilities do not give man control or lasting meaning
It removes man's limitations
It describes man's success in changing everything
challenge.explanation: After stressing human weakness, the passage says that many things increase vanity rather than solve it.
challenge.q: How does verse 11 continue the thought of verse 10?

answers: Limited people may occupy themselves with many things that do not change their condition
Limited people cannot think about anything
Many things make man stronger than reality
challenge.explanation: The verses connect human inability with the futility of multiplying pursuits.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between recognizing human limits and criticizing the multitude of things?

paragraphs.title: Uncertainty About the Good and the Future

answers: What is good for him in this life
How many people are in the world
Who is wise and who is foolish
easy.explanation: The verse asks, “For who knoweth what is good for man in this life?”
easy.q: What does man not know with certainty?

answers: A mountain
A shadow
A river
easy.explanation: The verse describes man's vain life as being spent “as a shadow.”
easy.q: What are the days of man's life compared to?

answers: What shall be after a man under the sun
What happened before his birth
How much labour he did in the past
easy.explanation: The verse asks who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun.
easy.q: What does no one know about the future?

answers: His life is fleeting and uncertain
He has no desires
He lives forever
medium.explanation: His vain life is spent as a shadow, making lasting certainty difficult.
medium.q: Why is it difficult for man to know what is good for him?

answers: In both matters man's knowledge is limited
Only the future is unknown; the good is always clear
Man knows both with certainty
medium.explanation: The verse asks both what is good in life and what will happen afterward.
medium.q: What connection does the verse make between uncertainty about good and uncertainty about the future?

answers: It passes away and lacks permanence
It lasts without end
It is filled with riches
medium.explanation: A shadow suggests brevity, change, and impermanence.
medium.q: What does the image of a shadow communicate about human life?

answers: Man must recognize that he cannot know the good and the future with certainty
Man can control everything that will happen
Wealth removes all uncertainty
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes the limits of human knowledge about life and what follows it.
challenge.q: What conclusion best fits the end of the chapter?

answers: It presents life as fleeting and impossible to hold securely
It shows that life is fixed and clear
It proves that man knows the future
challenge.explanation: A shadow moves and disappears, fitting the description of man's brief and uncertain life.
challenge.q: How does the image of a shadow strengthen the idea of uncertainty?

answers: To question man's ability to determine his highest good with certainty
To declare that everyone immediately knows the good
To show that the future is fully controllable
challenge.explanation: The question highlights man's limited understanding of both present good and future events.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the question, “Who knoweth what is good for man”?
